title: Late-Return Charge on Returned Repayments — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Training Bulletin
content:
A late-return charge on Benefit Overpayment Accounts recovers the depository's handling of an item the bank sent back after the normal return period, which comes back as a re-presented or disputed debit. It is added to the returned-payment fee when the bank took long to send the item back, counted in calendar days from the date the returned repayment was received to the date its return was booked.

| Calendar days from receipt of the repayment to the booking of its return | Charge added |
|---|---|
| More than 10 (the disputed-return days) | USD 20.00, the disputed-return charge |
| More than 5 (the late-return days) and no more than 10 | USD 5.00, the late-return charge |
| 5 or fewer | Nothing |

## Questions answered

**Which dates are compared?** The date the returned repayment was received is the booking date of the repayment entry on the overpayment's ledger carrying the returned confirmation number. The date its return was booked is the booking date of the return entry being charged, which is the most recent return entry booked on the overpayment.

**Is a gap of exactly 5 days late?** No. Five days or fewer add nothing; the late-return charge begins at 6 days.

**Is a gap of exactly 10 days a disputed return?** No. Ten days is no more than the disputed-return days, so it takes the late-return charge of USD 5.00; the disputed-return charge begins at 11 days.

## Boundary table (hypothetical dates)

| Repayment received | Return booked | Days | Charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 6 March | 5 | Nothing |
| 1 March | 7 March | 6 | USD 5.00 |
| 1 March | 11 March | 10 | USD 5.00 |
| 1 March | 12 March | 11 | USD 20.00 |
